text:
alex: CI alert on PR 8421 — microbench threshold diff triggered on kernel-selection test, seen on macstadium CI pool. cc @mira @sam :warning:
ci-bot: [benchmark-runner] PR 8421 failed perf guard: 
  test: runtime/kernel_selector_microbench
  metric: p50_latency_ms
  baseline: 4.3
  head: 5.9
  diff: +37% (threshold 15%)
  kv_cache_hit: baseline=0.92 head=0.67
  link: https://ci.internal/bench/8421/summary

mira: ugh, that kv hit drop is huge. any obvious changes in the PR?
alex: PR touches the seq-length sampler defaults (PR 8417 merged a few hours earlier). it changed the sample window to favor longer sequences for kernel heuristics training.
sam: that fits — our kernel selector fallback path picks a different kernel when expected seq len > 512. more long-seq samples could push the selector to prefer the long-seq kernels for short requests.
jordan: we should bisect between merge-base and PR 8417. quick check: running the CI microbench locally with and without the sampler change.
sam: running now, command I use: ```bash
make bench-ci TEST=kernel_selector_microbench REPEAT=5
```
ci-bot: queued bench job #2765 (sam)

sam: local results (5 runs): ```
baseline (no sampler-change): p50=4.2ms p95=9.8ms kv_hit=0.93
with-sampler-change: p50=5.8ms p95=12.4ms kv_hit=0.68
```

mira: confirms CI numbers. that's consistent. any idea why sampler would impact kv hit so much?
alex: my guess: the sampler change altered the histogram used at compile-time for kernel affinity and kv prefetch budgets. when affinity picked long-seq kernels they also changed KV allocation chunk sizes (less aggressive prefix caching) -> more misses.
jordan: I pulled a profile of a failing microbench run: ```
# top blockers by self time
- kv_lookup_loop 34%
- attention_kernel_short_seq 18%
- gather_prefetch 12%
```

mira: so kv lookups are dominating. did PR 8417 also change warmup or prefetch heuristics?
sam: it toggled a flag in runtime/config: seqlen_sampler.window=10000 -> 25000 and updated sample_weighting to exponential. that fed into the compilation heuristics job.
alex: action: bisect commit that introduced the sampler change in 8417 -> identify exact hunk that updated compile heuristics. I'll start a git bisect.
jordan: if bisect reproduces, we should either revert the sampler change or decouple sampler from compile heuristics until we add stability tests.
sam: small repro: toggling compile config to force prefer_short_kernels fixes perf locally: p50 back to 4.3ms, kv_hit=0.91. So a safe short-term revert is possible.
mira: open a revert PR for runtime/heuristics and mark it as rollout-blocker for Dedicated. I'll draft it.
alex: let's also add a targeted perf unit test that asserts kv_cache_hit > 0.85 for the microbench on PRs touching sampler/compile heuristics.
jordan: I'll add a CI golden that runs a smaller kv-hit smoke bench on merge windows.
sam: notes for the revert PR: include microbench output, profiler flamegraph, and a one-liner explaining the seqlen-sampler impact. make it clear this is a hotfix, followup will rework sampler->compile coupling.
mira: thanks. who will push the revert? alex?
alex: I'll open the revert PR now: PR 8423 (revert runtime: decouple sampler changes). tagging @oncall and @release.
ci-bot: created issue #3742 and PR 8423 by alex. queued for review.
mira: after revert lands, we'll monitor CI benchmarks across the fleet and schedule a postmortem to rework heuristics.
jordan: +1. also add an explanatory comment in the kernel selector code so future changes don't silently shift affinities. :memo:
alex: I'll update the perf playbook with bisect steps I used. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
